name: held
says: What holds each fast answer of layer 2's kernel (kernel.rs and outside.rs) that is not a placed question (those are held by the placed record): `record` the answers the record of the kernel against its translated module compares at every state (plan 79.46), and `exceptions` the answers nothing holds, each with its cause in words (plan 79.48 part F). A key is <trait or owner>::<name>; a free function has an empty owner. A line that no longer names an answer of the sources fails the test (tests/test_plan79_48.py).

record.Game::roles: the roles' names, by the side to move compared at every state
record.Game::initial: the start's fluents, compared at the first state of every game
record.Game::moves: the allowed moves as a set of the description's terms, at every state
record.Game::apply: the next state after every allowed move, as fluents
record.Game::outcome: whether the game has ended and the result
record.Game::move_name: the move's name as the description's term (`spec_term`), the moves compared as sets of terms
record.Game::base_facts: the state as fluents (the certificate of each game compares them with the oracle's fluents too)
record.::spec_term: the move's name as the description's term, the moves compared as sets of terms
record.DescriptionNames::description_name: the move's name as the description's term (it is `spec_term`)
record.KernelGame::state_facts: the state as fluents of the description, the one the record compares (bridge for every game)

exceptions.KernelGame::new: the kernel's own constructor (the library's variant and its start by number); the start it gives is compared at the first state of every game
exceptions.KernelGame::from_fen: a position read from the library's text notation of a position: a notation, not a rule; the positions it gives are the listed starts the small run begins from and the record compares from
exceptions.KernelGame::fen: the library's text notation of a position, for printing; no rule
exceptions.KernelGame::parse: the library's text notation of a move read on a position; no rule
exceptions.Game::name: the game's label; no rule
exceptions.Game::turn: the side to move read off the position with the end not asked (plan 79.39); the record compares `mover`, which is none at an end, so the side to move at an ended state is held by tests/test_plan79_39.py alone
exceptions.Game::key: a hash of the position's identity for the repeat tag; the description reads the game record as an input (`record`) and has no relation for a hash
exceptions.Game::captured: what a move takes as units removed (an explosion included): the description's `lifted` rows would answer it; not held yet (a plan after this one); the single unit a move takes is held under move_info
exceptions.Game::taken_at: what a move takes with the places it stood on: as `captured`; not held yet
exceptions.Game::changed: a unit changing kind by a move (a promotion): the description's `promotes` rows would answer it; not held yet
exceptions.Game::pass: the state with the side to move changed and nothing played, for the layers above: the description has no pass; the library builds the position
exceptions.Game::units: the units standing in the library's letters: a view of `cells`, which is held; the letters are not
exceptions.Placed::why_not: a diagnosis of why a step is refused, in the layers' own four words: the description has no relation that says it, and each word is a hand rule of the kernel's reading; held by tests/units_hand_checked.rs only
exceptions.Placed::without: a hypothetical board with a unit taken off (what depends on it made consistent; the library's refusal of a board): an edit of the board, not a question the description answers; held by tests/units_hand_checked_more.rs only
exceptions.Placed::relocate: a hypothetical board with a unit put elsewhere (the library's refusal of a board): an edit of the board; held by tests/units_hand_checked_more.rs only
exceptions.Starts::start_count: the number of starts of a game (960 for the game with a start by number): the description lists its starts in rules/variants/<game>.starts only for the game that has one; the numbering is the library's
exceptions.Starts::with_start: a start by its number (Scharnagl's numbering, kernel.rs): not a relation of the description
exceptions.StateText::state_text: the state as the library's text notation, keeping the passed-over place; a notation, not a rule
exceptions.StateText::read_state_text: a state read from the library's text notation; a notation, not a rule
exceptions.::chess960_fen: Scharnagl's numbering of the 960 starts (the library's); the start numbered 518 is compared at every game's first state and the listed starts are compared by the small run
exceptions.::uci_to_spec_term: the move's name in the description's notation, compared through `spec_term`, which calls it
